name: Herbal concoctions in pregnancy and to start labour
what_people_do: Women drink herbal mixtures through pregnancy, to induce labour or to boost health, often from family or friends, and often without telling the clinic.
why_they_say_it_works: To keep the pregnancy "strong", ease labour and avoid medicines.

documented_by.source: Herbal concoction usage before labor, urban Ghana, 2026, BMC Complement Med Ther, PMID 42928208
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Kumasi, 376 mothers: 95.6% knew of herbal concoctions, 17.9% used them; of users 34.3% used it to induce labour and 95.5% said it worked.

documented_by.source: Mothupi MC 2014, BMC Complement Altern Med, PMID 25370478
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Nairobi, 333 women: about 12% used herbal medicine in pregnancy; only 12.5% of users told health workers; used for back pain, toothache, indigestion and infections.

evidence.tested: Castor oil (a traditional labour inducer) by mouth
evidence.finding: No clear evidence of difference in caesarean rates; all who took it felt nauseous; trials too small to detect all but large differences.

source.name: Castor oil, bath and/or enema for induction of labour, Cochrane 2013, PMID 23881775

headline_tier_note: Tier D for the concoctions as a group; the castor oil line is a separate herb.
harm_note: Non-disclosure to clinicians means reactions are missed. The Cochrane castor oil review is a different herb from the concoctions studied.
gaps: Ingredients of Kumasi concoctions not extracted.
Maternal outcomes association in the Ghana paper not read.
